title.zh: 折返夷门：邯郸被围那年，一个不肯白送的人
title.en: Turning Back at the Yimen Gate: The Year Handan Was Besieged, and the Man Who Would Not Give It Away Free

dek.zh: 魏安釐王二十年，秦军围邯郸，魏王遣晋鄙救赵，大军未至（据简报转述）。魏公子决意赴秦军而死，出城后折返夷门，被一个守门老人当面点破：那是拿肉投餒虎。本文看他如何在没有干净选项时准备、付代价、认亏欠。
dek.en: In the twentieth year of King Anxi of Wei, Qin's armies closed around Handan and the king of Wei sent General Jin Bi to relieve Zhao, but the army never reached the city (retold from the briefing). The lord of Wei resolved to go and die at the Qin army; after riding out and turning back at the Yimen gate, an old gatekeeper cut him to his face: that is meat thrown to a starving tiger. Here is how he worked the problem when no option was clean — what he prepared, what it cost, and what he admitted he owed.

heading.en: Messengers Who Would Not Stop Coming

paras.zh: 魏安釐王二十年，秦军击破赵长平军之后，进兵围住邯郸。魏王派将军晋鄙带十万众救赵（留驻不进一节据简报转述，证据包无）——平原君的使者一批批赶到大梁，车盖接连不断，话一句比一句重：邯郸旦暮之间就要降秦，而魏国答应的救兵至今不到，公子不是自命能急人之困吗？末了还添一句「獨不憐公子姊邪」。公子无忌的姐姐，正是平原君夫人。
paras.en: In the twentieth year of King Anxi of Wei, after Qin had broken Zhao's army at Changping, its armies pressed on and encircled Handan. The king of Wei sent General Jin Bi with a hundred thousand troops to relieve Zhao (the halt of the relief army is retold from the briefing and is not in the evidence packet). Instead, envoys from Lord Pingyuan arrived in Daliang one after another — caps of office and carriage canopies in an unbroken line — each message harsher than the last: Handan was within days of surrendering to Qin, and the relief Wei had promised still had not come: was Lord Xinling not the man who prided himself on rushing to others in distress? The last message added a barb: "And have you no pity for your own sister?" Lord Xinling's elder sister was Lord Pingyuan's wife.

paras.zh: 更麻烦的是，魏王未再发兵、使人止晋鄙（据简报转述），而公子手里只有三千门客，未得国政之任。他决意赴秦军而死。出城路过夷门时，他向守门的侯生辞决。
paras.en: Worse still, the king of Wei sent no further troops and sent men to halt Jin Bi (retold from the briefing), and Lord Xinling had three thousand retainers but no appointment to the governance of the state. The plan he settled on was to go and die at the Qin army. On his way out of the city, passing the Yimen gate, he took his leave of Hou Ying, the gatekeeper.

heading.zh: 三千门客与一个守门人
heading.en: Three Thousand Retainers and One Gatekeeper

paras.zh: 公子无忌在魏国的名声，一半来自养客。《史记》说他「公子為人仁而下士，士無賢不肖皆謙而禮交之」，不敢以富贵骄士，以致食客三千人，方圆数千里的士人争相投奔。这些门客不只是排场：有一回他和魏王下棋，北境举烽报警，说赵寇将入界，公子说是赵王田猎，不久北边传话果然如此。魏王问何以知晓，他说门客中有人能得赵王阴事。
paras.en: Lord Xinling's standing in Wei rested half on his retainers. The Grand Historian writes that "he was humane and humble toward men of talent, treating every scholar, worthy or not, with courtesy and respect," never presuming on wealth and rank — so that he had three thousand retainers, and men of ability from a radius of several thousand li competed to attach themselves to him. They were not mere pageantry. One day, while he was playing a board game with the king of Wei, beacon fires on the northern frontier signaled a Zhao raid about to cross the border. The lord said the king of Zhao was out hunting, nothing more. Word later came from the north confirming exactly that. Asked how he knew, he explained that among his retainers was a man who could ferret out the king of Zhao's private business.

paras.zh: 一种解释是，这件事两面都算数：公子的信息能力得到验证，代价也记在账上——「是後魏王畏公子之賢能，不敢任公子以國政」。他越能干，魏王越不敢把国政交给他。等到邯郸告急，他未被任以国政，调兵无从谈起（作者推断）。
paras.en: Read the episode both ways. His intelligence was proven — and the price went straight onto the ledger: "From then on the king of Wei feared Lord Xinling's ability and dared not entrust him with the government of the state." The more capable he appeared, the less his king would hand him. By the time Handan cried for help he held no charge of the governance of the state, and raising troops was out of the question (the author's inference).

paras.zh: 公子敬重的另一个人，在夷门。侯嬴年七十，家贫，做大梁夷门的守门人。公子要厚赠，他不肯受，说自己「脩身絜行數十年，終不以監門困故而受公子財」。公子于是置酒大会宾客，空出车左的上位，亲自驾车去迎。侯生穿着破旧衣冠，径直上车坐了上座，不让，公子执辔愈恭。到家引他坐上座、遍赞宾客，满座皆惊。
paras.en: The other man Lord Xinling honored kept the Yimen — the eastern gate of Daliang. Hou Ying was seventy, poor, and gatekeeper there. Lord Xinling called on him and wanted to make him a handsome gift, but he would not accept: he had "kept himself and his conduct clean for decades," he said, "and would not take the lord's money just because a gatekeeper's life left him poor." So Lord Xinling laid on a feast for his assembled guests, and when everyone was seated he drove out himself with his carriage and escort, leaving the seat of honor at the left of the carriage empty, to fetch Hou Ying in person. The old man turned up in his shabby clothes and worn cap, climbed straight into the seat of honor without yielding it while Lord Xinling held the reins ever more respectfully. At home he seated Hou Ying in the place of honor and introduced him one by one to the assembled guests. The whole company was astonished.

paras.zh: 侯生后来把话说穿：他故意让公子的车骑久立市中，让过客围观，公子愈恭，于是「市人皆以嬴為小人，而以公子為長者能下士也」。他还推荐过一位屠者朱亥，说「此子賢者，世莫能知」。公子几次登门去请，朱亥不回谢，公子当时只觉得奇怪。这些看似闲棋的往来，邯郸被围那年全用上了。
paras.en: Hou Ying later spelled out the game he had been playing. He had deliberately left the lord's carriage standing in the marketplace so that passers-by could watch: the longer the lord waited, the more deferential he became — and so, he said, "the townsfolk all took me for a petty man, and the lord for a true elder who could humble himself before men of talent." He also recommended a butcher named Zhu Hai: "This is a worthy man; the world does not know him." Lord Xinling called on Zhu Hai several times; the butcher never came to return the courtesies, which the lord at that point simply found odd. All of these seemingly idle moves came due in the year Handan was besieged.

heading.en: From a Death Ride to Seizing an Army

paras.zh: 平原君的使者在大梁把话说绝：救兵不到，公子的高义安在。据简报转述，他先求魏王发兵不得，遂决意赴秦军而死。
paras.en: Lord Pingyuan's envoys left nothing to the imagination in Daliang: with no relief army in sight, where was the lord's famed righteousness? Retold from the briefing: he first appealed to the king of Wei for troops and was refused, and so resolved to go and die against the Qin army.

paras.zh: 那天他出城，路过夷门，见到侯生，把要去秦军送死的打算讲了，辞决而行。侯生只说一句「公子勉之矣，老臣不能從」。车行数里，公子心不快——这是《史记》的叙述用语——说：「吾所以待侯生者備矣，天下莫不聞，今吾且死而侯生曾無一言半辭送我，我豈有所失哉？」他「復引車還，問侯生」。
paras.en: That day he rode out, passed the Yimen gate, stopped to see Hou Ying and told him the whole plan — going to die at the Qin army — then took his leave and set off. Hou Ying said only: "Push on, my lord; this old servant cannot follow you." A few li on, the lord felt a gnawing unhappiness — the narrator's own phrase — and said: "I have treated Hou Ying handsomely in every way, as all the world knows; now I am going to my death, and Hou Ying has not half a word to say in seeing me off. Have I fallen short somewhere?" So he "turned his carriage around and went back to question Hou Ying."

paras.zh: 这一折返是全篇的转折。侯生当面把话挑明：「今有難，無他端而欲赴秦軍，譬若以肉投餒虎，何功之有哉」——没有别的办法，只想冲进秦军，等于拿肉喂饿虎，白送，还要门客何用。他还说，正因为知道公子待他厚，此去而不相送，公子必会「恨之復返」。他自己说：「以是知公子恨之復返也」。
paras.en: That turn is the pivot of the whole story. Hou Ying put it to his face: "With disaster upon you and no plan at all, you mean to throw yourself at the Qin army — that is like throwing meat to a starving tiger. What would it accomplish?" Nothing gained, and the retainers squandered besides. He added that he had counted on exactly this: knowing how well the lord treated him, going to die without so much as a parting word would make the lord "resent it and come back." In Hou Ying's own words, he said as much: he knew the lord would resent it and come back.

paras.zh: 侯生给出的方案：晋鄙的兵符常在魏王卧内，如姬最幸，出入卧内，有办法窃取。如姬的父亲被人所杀，三年未能报仇，她曾向公子泣诉，公子使客斩了仇人的头敬献给她。原文记如姬「欲為公子死，無所辭，顧未有路耳」，所以开口请她，她必许。得虎符、夺晋鄙军，北救赵而西却秦，「此五霸之伐也」。
paras.en: Hou Ying's plan: the tally that authorized Jin Bi to move troops — a tiger tally — was normally kept in the king of Wei's bedchamber, and Lady Ruji, the king's favorite, came and went there and was able to steal it. Her father had been murdered; for three years she had sought revenge. She had wept to Lord Xinling, who sent a retainer to cut off her enemy's head and presented it to her respectfully. The source has her ready to die for Lord Xinling and to refuse him nothing; only "she had no way to repay him." If the lord would but ask, she would certainly agree. Then, with the tiger tally in hand, seize Jin Bi's army, relieve Zhao in the north and drive Qin back in the west: "that is an achievement to rank with the Five Hegemons."

paras.zh: 计策只管前半，后半是坏情况。侯生提醒「將在外，主令有所不受」：就算合符成功，晋鄙不交兵权、再向魏王请示，事情就危险了。带上屠者朱亥，「晉鄙聽，大善；不聽，可使擊之」。公子听完流泪，说「晉鄙嚄唶宿將，往恐不聽，必當殺之，是以泣耳，豈畏死哉」——哭的是非杀本国老将不可，不是怕死。朱亥说自己是市井鼓刀屠者，从前不回谢是以为小礼无所用，「今公子有急，此乃臣效命之秋也」。侯生此前已说过老臣不能从，这里只请数着公子的行程，到晋鄙军那天「北鄉自剄，以送公子」。
paras.en: The plan covered only the first half; the second half was the bad case. Hou Ying warned that "a general in the field is not bound by every order from his sovereign": even with the tallies matching, if Jin Bi withheld the army and sent to the king instead, the whole enterprise would be in danger. So take the butcher Zhu Hai along: "If Jin Bi obeys, excellent; if not, you may have him strike." Lord Xinling wept on hearing it: "Jin Bi is a battle-seasoned old general; I fear he will not obey, and then he must be killed. That is why I weep. Do you imagine I fear death?" What he cried for was the killing of his own country's veteran commander, not the risk to himself. Zhu Hai said he was a butcher who slapped the knife in the marketplace; he had never returned the lord's visits because "petty courtesies were of no use" — but "now that the lord is in a tight spot, this is the hour to spend my life." Hou Ying, who had already said at the gate that he was too old to follow, here only asked to count the days of the journey, so that "on the day you reach Jin Bi's camp I shall face north and cut my own throat, to see you off."

paras.zh: 到了晋鄙军中，公子矫魏王令代晋鄙。合符之后，晋鄙不肯交权（此节据简报转述）。朱亥袖中四十斤铁椎，椎杀晋鄙。公子遂将晋鄙军，随即勒兵下令：「父子俱在軍中，父歸；兄弟俱在軍中，兄歸；獨子無兄弟，歸養。」得选兵八万人，进兵击秦军。
paras.en: At Jin Bi's camp, Lord Xinling announced that he came on the king's orders to replace Jin Bi. The tallies matched, but Jin Bi refused to hand over his command (this episode is retold from the briefing). Zhu Hai produced a forty-catty iron mallet from his sleeve and killed him. Lord Xinling then took command of Jin Bi's army and immediately issued an order to the troops: "Fathers and sons both serving: the father goes home. Brothers both serving: the elder goes home. An only son with no brothers: go home and support your parents." He selected eighty thousand men and advanced against the Qin army.

paras.zh: 秦军解去，邯郸得救，赵国保住。赵王与平原君亲到边界迎接，平原君背着箭袋在前引路，赵王再拜说「自古賢人未有及公子者也」，平原君不敢自比于人。
paras.en: The Qin army broke off and withdrew. Handan was relieved, Zhao preserved. The king of Zhao and Lord Pingyuan came out to the border to receive him in person, Lord Pingyuan carrying the quiver and arrow-case and leading the way. The king of Zhao bowed twice and said: "Of worthies since ancient times, none has been the lord's equal." At that moment Lord Pingyuan dared not compare himself with anyone.

paras.zh: 赵孝成王感念公子矫夺晋鄙兵存赵，与平原君商量以五城相封。公子的反应是「意驕矜而有自功之色」——仍是叙述用语。门客劝他：别人对公子的恩不可忘，公子对别人的恩最好忘掉；况且矫魏王令、夺晋鄙兵救赵，「於趙則有功矣，於魏則未為忠臣也」，自骄而居功，不可取。公子立自责，似若无所容者。
paras.en: King Xiaocheng of Zhao, grateful that Lord Xinling had overridden the general and seized the army to save Zhao, took counsel with Lord Pingyuan about granting him five cities. The lord's reaction, in the narrator's phrasing, was "a look of pride and self-congratulation." A retainer told him: some things must not be forgotten, others must be. Kindness done to the lord he should remember; kindness the lord has done to others, he should forget. And besides, overriding the king's order and seizing the army to save Zhao was "a service to Zhao, but not the act of a loyal minister to Wei" — to swagger over such a credit was beneath him. The lord at once blamed himself, looking as if he had nowhere to hide.

paras.zh: 魏王怒公子盗兵符、矫杀晋鄙，公子自己清楚。退秦存赵之后，他让将领把军队带回魏国，自己与门客留在赵国。这场救赵中盗符夺军、矫杀晋鄙的一段没有魏王的授权。
paras.en: The king of Wei was furious that his tally had been stolen and Jin Bi killed on a forged order, and Lord Xinling knew it. Having driven off Qin and saved Zhao, he sent the generals back to Wei with the army and stayed behind in Zhao with his retainers. The part of the rescue of Zhao in which he stole the tally, seized the army and killed Jin Bi carried no royal authorization..

paras.zh: 把整件事拆开看，公子一次也不是在好与坏之间挑，摆在面前的是几个都不干净的做法：求魏王（走不通，据简报转述）、赴秦军而死（侯生斥为「以肉投餒虎」）、矫令夺军（侯生所献，伤本国）。作者推断，侯生那句「以肉投餒虎」的作用，是逼他把勇气换成方案。作者提出的反事实：若他不折返，多半带着门客死在秦军阵前，邯郸未必得救，也不会有后来那支进兵的军队。
paras.en: Take the whole affair apart and the lord is never choosing between good and bad; what stood before him were courses of action that were all dirty: appeal to the king (a dead end, retold from the briefing), ride to die at the Qin army (which Hou Ying called throwing meat to a starving tiger), forge an order and seize the army (proposed by Hou Ying; a wound to his own state). The author's inference is that Hou Ying's line about throwing meat to a starving tiger is what forced him to trade courage for a plan. The author's counterfactual: had he not turned back, he would most likely have died with his retainers in front of the Qin lines, Handan might never have been relieved, and there would have been no army marching against Qin afterward.

paras.zh: 第二处是把坏情况写进计划。侯生提醒将在外、主令有所不受，于是朱亥随行、袖中藏椎，晋鄙听则已，不听则击。作者推断，这一步的难处不在敢不敢：公子听后的反应是流泪说必杀晋鄙，自己并非怕死。从结果看，他欠了自己这方一笔债——杀本国宿将、盗王符、绝于魏王——仍然把方案走完。原文未写他事前是否权衡，能记的只有这句答话。
paras.en: The second undignified spot is writing the bad case into the plan. Hou Ying's reminder that a general in the field need not accept every order put Zhu Hai at his side with a mallet up his sleeve: if Jin Bi complied, well; if not, strike. The author's inference: the hard part here was not daring. The lord's response on hearing the plan was tears — he said Jin Bi had to be killed, and that he was not afraid to die. In the outcome he took on a debt to his own side — killing his country's veteran commander, stealing the king's tally, breaking with the king — and he went through with it anyway. Whether he weighed this beforehand goes unrecorded; the only thing on the record is that answer.

paras.zh: 第三处是事后的账。门客那句「於趙則有功矣，於魏則未為忠臣也」把两边算清：功劳是赵国的，亏欠是魏国的。原文只记他立自责，未记辩解之辞，随后遣军归魏、自己留赵，用离开把这笔债认下来（作者推断，原文只写留赵这一行为）。一种解释是，他不居功的姿态与事后自责相呼应：赵王、平原君边界亲迎在前，门客劝谏、公子自责、留赵在后。
paras.en: The third is the accounting afterward. The retainer's words — "a service to Zhao, but not the act of a loyal minister to Wei" — keep both columns straight: the credit belongs to Zhao, the debt to Wei. The source records only that he blamed himself on the spot, and nothing of any argument; then send the army home and stay in Zhao, acknowledging the debt through departure (the author's inference; the source records only the act of staying in Zhao). One reading: his refusal to claim credit chimes with the self-blame that followed — the welcome at the border came first, and the retainer's rebuke, the self-reproach, and staying in Zhao came after.

paras.zh: 今天最常见的版本是：团队看到明显风险，决策层因为怕更大的对手压着不动。你手里有一线证据，也有一个能干的人。先别急着感动自己——照侯生的话问一句，我这个动作是解决问题，还是拿肉投餒虎？如果只是冲出去把话说完、把人得罪完，而风险一点没减，那叫白送。
paras.en: The commonest modern version: a team sees a clear risk, while the people with authority freeze for fear of a bigger opponent. You hold a piece of hard evidence and you know a capable person. Before you start admiring your own nerve, put Hou Ying's question to your plan: is this move solving the problem, or throwing meat to a starving tiger? If all it does is get you out there to say your piece and offend everyone while the risk sits exactly where it was, that is a free throwaway.

paras.zh: 若决定动手，就把“对方不配合”写进计划：谁在什么情况下顶上，最坏的结果谁兜，留下什么记录。事情成了、庆功的时候，别急着站到中间：被绕过的流程、替你签字的人、被架空的上级，都是一笔账。把“于某处有功、于某处未为忠”先自己说出口，比等别人替你说体面得多。
paras.en: If you decide to act, write "the other side may not cooperate" into the plan: who steps in under which circumstances, who covers the worst outcome, what record stays behind. And when it works and the celebration starts, do not rush to stand in the middle. The process you bypassed, the person who signed for you, the superior you left out of the loop — all of that is an account. Saying it yourself first — a service here, a disloyalty there — is far more dignified than waiting for someone else to say it for you.

heading.en: Where Not to Take It at Face Value

paras.zh: 先说史源。本篇只有一个来源——《史记·魏公子列传》一篇，无旁证可对。文中的密语与对话，如侯嬴献窃符之计、朱亥答话，是史家的记述，未必逐字。公子的「心不快」「意驕矜」「立自責」都是叙述用语，不是实录的心理。纪年照原文写魏安釐王二十年，不换算公元。
paras.en: Start with the sources. This piece rests on a single source: the "Hereditary House of Lord Wei" in the Records of the Grand Historian, with no corroboration to set against it. The whispered schemes and dialogue — Hou Ying's plan to steal the tally, Zhu Hai's reply — are the historian's rendering and need not be verbatim. The lord's "unease," "self-congratulation," and "blaming himself" are narrative labels, not recorded psychology. The year is given as the twentieth of King Anxi of Wei, as the source has it, with no conversion to the common era.

paras.zh: 细节上更该存疑的是：「得選兵八萬人」这个数字只此一处，无旁证；晋鄙军中合符如何校验、杀将之后如何收场，原文没有记载；侯生自刭的动机、如姬盗符之后的下落，原文只写行为和一句话，没有更多交代。此外，本文转述的几处关键过程——魏王使人止晋鄙留军观望、公子约车骑欲赴秦军、如姬盗出兵符、晋鄙合符起疑——所据摘录未通过逐字核对，只作转述，不引原文。
paras.en: The detail most worth doubting: the figure of "eighty thousand picked men" appears here alone, with no corroboration; how the tallies were verified in Jin Bi's camp and how the affair wound up after the killing of the general go unrecorded; Hou Ying's motive in cutting his own throat, and Lady Ruji's fate after stealing the tally, come down to an act and a single sentence, with nothing further. In addition, several key turns retold here — the king sending men to stop Jin Bi and hold the army in wait-and-see, the lord gathering chariots to go and die against Qin, Lady Ruji stealing the tally, Jin Bi growing suspicious when the tallies matched — rest on extracts that have not been checked word for word, and are retold rather than quoted.

scenario.zh: 小区电梯多次故障，你拿到一份检测报告，写明主板隐患明显；物业经理因怕得罪开发商不肯停用报修，只答应“再观察”。邻居里有一位相熟的电梯维修工愿意帮忙，但走正常报批要等一个月。
scenario.en: The elevator in your building has broken down several times. You have an inspection report stating plainly that the main control board is dangerously defective. The property manager, afraid of offending the developer, refuses to take the elevator out of service for repairs and will only agree to "keep watching it." Among the residents is an elevator technician you know who is willing to help — but going through the proper approval route would take a month.

question.zh: 在“上面不动、下面要出事”的局面里，你会不会绕过物业直接动手？动手之前，你会先备好什么，来对付“对方不配合”这一步？事成之后，你打算怎么向物业和被绕过的规则交代这笔账？
question.en: In a situation where those above will not move and those below are heading for an accident, would you bypass the property manager and act directly? Before acting, what would you prepare in advance to handle the step where "the other side does not cooperate"? And once it is done, how do you account to the property manager and to the rules you bypassed?

assumptions.zh:
隐患是真的，且有书面检测报告可留证
维修工愿意帮忙，但无授权，动手即属违规
物业不会主动认错，也不会替你担责
assumptions.en:
The defect is real, and the written inspection report can be kept as evidence
The technician is willing to help, but has no authorization; acting without it is a violation
The property manager will not admit fault, and will not take responsibility for you

steps.zh:
先判性质：直接停用或硬闯，是不是侯生说的“以肉投餒虎”——无人配合、报告不被承认，风险一点没减
为坏情况备预案：维修工到场而物业阻拦时，谁签字、谁见证、保留什么记录
把代价列清：可能被追责的人名单，以及最坏结果由谁兜
事成后不居功，主动承认绕过流程这笔亏欠，把整改记录和检测报告一并交给物业归档
steps.en:
Judge the nature of the act first: shutting it down by force, or barging in — is that Hou Ying's "meat thrown to a starving tiger"? If nobody cooperates and the report is not accepted, the risk has not shrunk at all
Prepare for the bad case: if the technician arrives and the property manager blocks the work, who signs, who witnesses, what records are preserved
Lay out the costs clearly: the list of people who might be held responsible, and who covers the worst outcome
Afterwards, do not claim credit; volunteer the admission that you bypassed procedure, and hand the repair records and the inspection report to the property manager for filing

alternative.zh: 作者提出的替代选择：先把报告公开给全体业主，把风险转成集体决定，用共同压力替个人冒险。代价是慢，可能来不及；好处是不必由一个人背“矫令杀将”的账。
alternative.en: The author's proposed alternative: publish the report to all the owners first, turning the risk into a collective decision and using shared pressure instead of personal daring. The cost is slowness — it may come too late; the benefit is that no single person has to carry the account of "forging the order and killing the general."

uncertainty_note.zh: 本篇只有一个史源（《史记·魏公子列传》一处记述），密语与对话是史家记述，未必逐字；「心不快」「意驕矜」「立自責」是叙述用语而非实录心理；不换算公元年份；“得选兵八万人”仅此一处、无旁证；晋鄙军中如何收场、合符如何校验原文未载；侯生自刭的动机、如姬盗符的后续原文只写行为与一句话。另有几处关键过程所据摘录未通过逐字核对（魏王止晋鄙、公子约车骑赴死、如姬盗符、晋鄙合符起疑），本文只作转述、不引原文。
uncertainty_note.en: This piece rests on a single historical source (one account in the "Hereditary House of Lord Wei" in the Records of the Grand Historian). The whispered schemes and dialogue are the historian's rendering and need not be verbatim; "unease," "self-congratulation," and "blaming himself" are narrative labels rather than recorded psychology; years are not converted to the common era; "eighty thousand picked men" appears in this one place with no corroboration; how the tallies were verified and how the affair ended in Jin Bi's camp are unrecorded in the source; Hou Ying's motive for cutting his own throat and Lady Ruji's story after stealing the tally are given only as an act and a single sentence. Several key processes retold here (the king stopping Jin Bi, the lord gathering chariots to go and die, Lady Ruji stealing the tally, Jin Bi growing suspicious at the matching of the tallies) rest on extracts that have not been verified word for word, and are retold here without quotation.

preheader.zh: 偷符之前，他先折回去问了看门的老头一句
preheader.en: Before stealing the tally, he turned back and asked the old gatekeeper one question
